fields.document_title: WISHBONE System-on-Chip (SoC) Interconnection Architecture for Portable IP Cores
fields.ipr_status: Public domain — Notice: the document is not copyrighted in any restrictive sense and has been placed into the public domain. The names 'WISHBONE' and 'WISHBONE COMPATIBLE' rubber stamp logo are placed into the public domain (within the scope of System-on-Chip design, System-on-Chip fabrication, and related areas of commercial use). Royalty-free; the specification may be used for the design and production of SoC components without royalties or other financial obligations to OpenCores.
fields.intended_audience: Hardware engineers integrating, designing, and verifying SoC IP cores; IP core developers; SoC integrators; reuse-oriented design teams (small, medium, and large).
fields.purpose: Defines a flexible, open, royalty-free SoC interconnection architecture for portable IP cores. Wishbone enables design reuse by providing a common interface specification that alleviates SoC integration problems, improves system portability and reliability, and reduces time-to-market.
key_features: Simple, compact, logical IP core hardware interfaces that require very few logic gates
Supports structured design methodologies used by large project teams
Full set of popular data transfer bus protocols including READ/WRITE cycle, BLOCK transfer cycle, RMW (read-modify-write) cycle
Modular data bus widths and operand sizes up to 64-bits
Supports both BIG ENDIAN and LITTLE ENDIAN data ordering
Variable core interconnection methods: point-to-point, shared bus, crossbar switch, data flow interconnection, and off-chip
Handshaking protocol allows each IP core to throttle its data transfer speed
Supports single-clock data transfers (single clock-edge operation, synchronous)
Supports normal cycle termination [ACK], retry termination [RTY], and termination due to error [ERR]
Modular address widths (parameterizable)
Partial address decoding scheme for SLAVEs — facilitates high-speed address decoding, less redundant logic, supports variable address sizing and interconnection means
User-defined tags (TGA / TGD / TGC) for applying information to an address bus, data bus, or bus cycle — useful for data transfers, parity / error correction, interrupt vectors, cache control
MASTER / SLAVE architecture for very flexible system designs
Multiprocessing (multi-MASTER) capabilities; arbitration methodology defined by the end user (priority arbiter, round-robin arbiter, etc.)
Synchronous design assures portability, simplicity and ease of use
Very simple, variable timing specification (single-clock edge-triggered)
Independent of hardware technology (FPGA, ASIC, etc.)
Independent of delivery method (soft, firm, or hard core)
Independent of synthesis tool, router, and layout tool technology
Independent of FPGA and ASIC test methodologies
Seamless design progression between FPGA prototypes and ASIC production chips
Backward-compatible Wishbone Registered Feedback bus cycles (B.4 addition) for advanced synchronous cycle termination + higher throughput burst transfers using CTI / BTE tags
interconnection_topologies: Point-to-point — single MASTER + single SLAVE, simplest connection
Shared bus — single MASTER multi-SLAVE (or multi-MASTER) sharing a common bus with arbitration
Crossbar switch — multiple MASTERs to multiple SLAVEs with parallel channels for higher aggregate throughput
Data flow interconnection — IP cores in a pipelined sequential flow (each core has both SLAVE and MASTER interfaces); parallelism via concurrent execution stages
Off-chip interconnection — extends Wishbone to chip-to-chip I/O routing

signaling_summary.clock: Single CLK_I per Wishbone interface; rising-edge sampled (single-clock synchronous protocol). [CLK_O] generated by SYSCON module, distributed to [CLK_I] of all MASTER and SLAVE interfaces.
signaling_summary.reset: Single RST_I per Wishbone interface (active HIGH). [RST_O] generated by SYSCON module, distributed to [RST_I] of all MASTER and SLAVE interfaces.
signaling_summary.logic_levels: All Wishbone interface signals MUST use active HIGH logic (Rule 2.30). Lower-case 'n' or '#' / '/' prefix not used for naming active-LOW signals.
signaling_summary.signal_naming: All signal names use the '_I' (input to the core) or '_O' (output from the core) suffix; e.g. [ACK_I] is an input and [ACK_O] is an output. Signal arrays use parenthesis notation [DAT_I(63..0)].
signaling_summary.naming_anchor: Signal names are referenced inside [ ] brackets to distinguish them from prose. MASTER signal names are used as the canonical reference unless otherwise noted.

fields.vendor: OpenCores Organization (steward) / Silicore Corporation (original author Wade D. Peterson)
fields.logo: WISHBONE COMPATIBLE rubber-stamp logo MAY be affixed to SoC components that are 100% compliant with this specification (PERMISSION 1.00).
fields.package_info_rationale: Wishbone B4 is a bus protocol specification and is independent of hardware technology (FPGA / ASIC). No package, pinout, or electrical-DC data exists in this document.
fields.electrical_specs_rationale: The specification defines only logical, single-clock, synchronous signal semantics (Chapter 6 Timing Specification: only Tpd,clk-su = 1/Fclk constraint per signal path). It is explicitly independent of logic signaling levels (1.2 WISHBONE Objectives — 'to make WISHBONE interfaces independent of logic signaling levels'). No voltage / current / IO-standard information is part of the protocol.

specification_keyword_semantics.RULE: Basic framework — MUST be followed to ensure compatibility between interfaces. Reserved upper-case words: MUST and MUST NOT.
specification_keyword_semantics.RECOMMENDATION: Advice — designers would be wise to take; ignoring may cause performance or integration problems.
specification_keyword_semantics.SUGGESTION: Helpful but not vital advice for designers who have not yet gained experience.
specification_keyword_semantics.PERMISSION: Reassures that a certain approach is acceptable and will not cause problems. Reserved upper-case word: MAY.
specification_keyword_semantics.OBSERVATION: Clarifies or gives rationale; does not offer specific advice.

tag_types.description: Address tag — user-defined information attached to address (e.g. parity, address size, protected memory)
Address tag input (SLAVE-side mirror of TGA_O)
Data tag, input — info qualified with the data input array
Data tag, output — info qualified with the data output array (e.g. parity / ECC / time stamp)
Cycle tag (output) — info attached to the bus cycle (e.g. SINGLE / BLOCK / RMW discrimination, interrupt acknowledge, cache control)
Cycle tag (input) — SLAVE-side mirror of TGC_O

cycle_types_classic: Classic Standard BLOCK READ Cycle (3.3.1) — multiple READ phases bundled in a single CYC_O assertion
Classic Pipelined BLOCK READ Cycle (3.3.1 alt example)
Classic Pipelined BLOCK WRITE Cycle (3.3.2 alt example)
RMW (Read-Modify-Write) Cycle (3.4) — atomic read then write to same address in a single CYC_O
fields.endianness_default: Not mandated by the spec — both BIG ENDIAN and LITTLE ENDIAN data organizations are supported and MUST be declared in the WISHBONE DATASHEET (Rule 2.15 item 10). When port size = granularity, BIG ENDIAN and LITTLE ENDIAN transfers are identical, and the interface shall be specified as BIG/LITTLE ENDIAN.

evidence.quote: Stewardship is maintained by OpenCores Organization (rherveille@opencores.org / www.opencores.org). Notice is hereby given that this document is not copyrighted, and has been placed into the public domain. The name 'WISHBONE' and the 'WISHBONE COMPATIBLE' rubber stamp logo are hereby placed into the public domain within the scope of System-on-Chip design, System-on-Chip fabrication and related areas of commercial use. This specification may be used for the design and production of System-on-Chip (SoC) components without royalties or other financial obligations to OpenCores.

Wade D. Peterson from Silicore Corporation is the original author and steward. The various revisions of the WISHBONE specification, along with their changes and revision history, can be found at www.silicore.net/wishbone.htm.

The WISHBONE System-on-Chip (SoC) Interconnection Architecture for Portable IP Cores is a flexible design methodology for use with semiconductor IP cores. Its purpose is to foster design reuse by alleviating System-on-Chip integration problems.

Simple, compact, logical IP core hardware interfaces that require very few logic gates. Full set of popular data transfer bus protocols including: READ/WRITE cycle, BLOCK transfer cycle, RMW cycle. Modular data bus widths and operand sizes up to 64-bits. Supports both BIG ENDIAN and LITTLE ENDIAN data ordering. Variable core interconnection methods support point-to-point, shared bus, crossbar switch, and switched fabric interconnections. Handshaking protocol allows each IP core to throttle its data transfer speed. Supports single clock data transfers. Supports normal cycle termination, retry termination and termination due to error. Modular address widths. Partial address decoding scheme for SLAVEs. User-defined tags. MASTER / SLAVE architecture. Multiprocessing (multi-MASTER) capabilities. Arbitration methodology is defined by the end user (priority arbiter, round-robin arbiter, etc.). Synchronous design assures portability, simplicity and ease of use. Independent of hardware technology (FPGA, ASIC, etc.). Independent of delivery method (soft, firm or hard core). Seamless design progression between FPGA prototypes and ASIC production chips.

Five keywords: RULE, RECOMMENDATION, SUGGESTION, PERMISSION, OBSERVATION. All rules MUST be followed to ensure compatibility between interfaces. The upper-case words MUST and MUST NOT are reserved exclusively for stating rules.
All WISHBONE interface signals MUST use active high logic.

All signal names used in this specification have the '_I' or '_O' characters attached to them. These indicate if the signals are an input (to the core) or an output (from the core). For example, [ACK_I] is an input and [ACK_O] is an output.

Table 3-1 TAG TYPEs: Address tag TGA_O()/TGA_I() associated with ADR_O()/ADR_I(). Data tag input TGD_I() associated with DAT_I(). Data tag output TGD_O() associated with DAT_O(). Cycle tag TGC_O()/TGC_I() associated with the Bus Cycle.

CTI_O(2:0): 000 Classic cycle; 001 Constant address burst cycle; 010 Incrementing burst cycle; 011/100/101/110 Reserved; 111 End-of-Burst. BTE_IO(1:0): 00 Linear burst; 01 4-beat wrap burst; 10 8-beat wrap burst; 11 16-beat wrap burst.
